context: A police officer answers a teen reporter's questions after a storm
purpose: Teach: 嵐/被災/消防/役所/解体/区域/警官/侵入

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 警官として、昨夜の嵐の被害をどう見ていますか？
lines.en: As a police officer, how do you see last night's storm damage?
lines.style: polite interview opener, slightly nervous teen reporter tone

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 正直、想像以上だ。被災された方も多くて、今も消防の救助活動が続いている。
lines.en: Honestly, worse than expected. Many were affected, and fire crews are still rescuing people.
lines.style: calm, weary authority voice, measured pacing, official tone

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 区役所には、もう相談に行った住民はいるんでしょうか？
lines.en: Have any residents already gone to the ward office to consult?
lines.style: curious follow-up question, polite formal register

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: ああ、朝から長い列だよ。倒れた家屋の解体工事についての問い合わせが特に多いね。
lines.en: Yeah, a long line since morning. Lots of questions about demolition work for collapsed houses.
lines.style: informative explanation with mild sigh, professional concern

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: 危険区域への立ち入りは、まだ禁止されているんですか？
lines.en: Is entry into the danger zones still being prohibited?
lines.style: earnest probing question, notebook-in-hand reporter energy

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: もちろんだ。許可なく入れば不法侵入になる。君も絶対に近づかないでくれよ。
lines.en: Of course. Entering without permission is trespassing. Don't go anywhere near it, please.
lines.style: firm warning, protective elder tone, direct eye-contact feel

lines.speaker: sakura_teen
lines.jp: わかりました。最後に、町の皆さんへ一言お願いできますか？
lines.en: Understood. Lastly, could you say a word to the town's residents?
lines.style: respectful closing question, slightly softer voice

lines.speaker: takeda_officer
lines.jp: 焦らず、無理せず。困ったら必ず役所か警察に連絡してほしい。
lines.en: Don't rush, don't push yourselves. If you're in trouble, contact the office or police.
lines.style: sincere closing message, warm but authoritative delivery
